messages:
maria: heads up — LumenGo (dedicated-prod-3) hit a sudden TPS surge around 2026-03-17T17:10Z. We're seeing token-per-second SLO violations and lots of 429s coming from admission_control. sample request_id=rq_7f8e3a2b
monitoring-bot: alert: dedicated-prod-3 · admission_control rejects ↑ (5m) · 429 spike · link: https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/dedicated-prod-3
kevin: @maria can you paste the last_request_id and whether burst_credits were exhausted? Also what's the autoscaler state (scaled_at / cooldown)?
maria: last_request_id=rq_7f8e3a2b, burst_credits remaining=0/600, autoscaler state: in_cooldown=true, scaled_at=1772003150, min_replicas=2, max_replicas=6, cooldown_seconds=300
maria: log snippet from admission controller:
```
[17:10:42] admission_control: reject request_id=rq_7f8e3a2b reason=admission_threshold_exceeded pool=dedicated-prod-3
[17:10:45] admission_control: metric token_rate=1250 tps target=1000 headroom_pct=5 burst_credits=0
```
sophie: checking the dashboards — sustained 120% of target for ~3m, headroom is only 5% for this pool. That explains the hard rejects. Recommendation: bump headroom_pct -> 20% for this pool to avoid immediate rejections on short surges. :thinking_face:
ryan: short-term mitigation: switch to soft admission policy so we shed background/low-priority work first instead of hard 429s. config suggestion:
```
admission_policy: soft
soft_threshold_pct: 20
throttle_classes:
  - class: background
    action: delay/queue
  - class: interactive
    action: allow
```
This will keep interactive flows alive while degrading lower priority jobs.
june-sre: if LumenGo is on a Dedicated SLA we can emergency-scale to 4 replicas. Command:
`redwoodctl clusters scale dedicated-prod-3 --replicas 4 --reason "LumenGo emergency TPS surge"`
I'll run this once we confirm from support. Note: scaling reserved capacity may have billing/commit implications — ping finance if this goes >24h. :thumbsup:
maria: please run the scale, June. I'll notify the customer: "We're scaling your pool to restore SLOs; you should see improvement within ~60-90s. We're also adjusting admission policy to reduce hard 429s."
ryan: medium-term: increase burst_credits capacity and regen rate for PLG-heavy customers. Example:
```
burst_credits:
  capacity: 1200
  regen_per_second: 6
```
Also add a short admission grace window to let autoscaler respond to sub-5m surges.
kevin: post-incident TODOs (assign owners):
- Headroom policy review (sophie) — ensure pools with spiky traffic get >15% headroom
- Burst credits defaults (ryan) — raise defaults for PLG workloads
- Autoscaler tuning (june-sre) — reduce cooldown for ephemeral surges or add fast-path scale-up
- Runbook update (maria) — customer comms + repro steps
support-bot: ticket SUP-4452 created, linked to customer case LUM-1987 and oncall page.
maria: thanks — I'll collect repro steps and attach request traces + logs to SUP-4452. Will follow up with CSM. :eyes:
kevin: one more: let's consider admission_control metrics alert that includes headroom_pct and burst_credits_remaining so support can triage before customers see 429s.
sophie: agreed. I'll add a Grafana panel and an alert rule draft.
june-sre: scaling completed — replicas -> 4 at 1772003565. Observing token rate normalize; 429s dropping. Monitoring for 10m before closing.
maria: closing loop with LumenGo: message sent to CSM and engineering contact. Will update SUP-4452 with final timeline and config diffs.
